clue.text: Corporal drunk in charge when guarding master

indicators.note: a guard stands around what it protects, so one piece is wrapped around another

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
MA, Master of Arts, is a master's degree
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A drunken army corporal who was on duty guarding his superior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporal' looks like the soldier but is the adjective meaning bodily. The drunk wraps round the master, and IC follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporal as an adjective means relating to the physical body, which is exactly the meaning of somatic in medicine and biology.

clue.text: Primarily sold packed lunches in fast food joint

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.clueFragment: sold packed lunches in fast food
blocks.note: the initials of these six words

explanation.surface: A fast food outlet that mainly sold packed lunches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast food joint' reads as one phrase, but 'joint' stands alone as the definition in its drug sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A spliff is slang for a cannabis cigarette, which is also commonly called a joint.

clue.text: Tricky staff?

blocks.note: surface reading: employees who are difficult to manage
setter's reading: a stick or rod used for performing tricks, as a conjuror does

explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' suggests workers, but a staff is also a stick; a trickster's stick is the conjuror's prop.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror performs tricks with a short rod, so a stick used for tricks is a playful description of it.

clue.text: Hollow skins left in Tuesday’s scraps

indicators.note: a hollow thing has its inside removed, so only the outside letters stay
one thing placed inside another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: TUES is the usual abbreviation of the day; it is split to take the others
the first and last letters of the word
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Empty skins discarded among the leftovers from Tuesday's meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scraps' looks like leftover food, but it is the plural noun for fights. The day's usual three-day abbreviation plus S is split open to take the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraps in the informal sense are fights or scuffles, and tussles are vigorous struggles of the same kind.

clue.text: Attendants from Europe breaking frame I chucked out

indicators.note: to break into something is to get inside it, so one piece enters another
something chucked out is thrown away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a chassis is the base frame of a vehicle
the letter to be thrown out of the frame
EUR is an abbreviation for Europe

explanation.surface: Staff from the continent smashing a picture frame and throwing it out.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the I leaves CHASSS, and EUR breaks in before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasseur is a uniformed hotel attendant or footman, the French word used in English for such liveried servants.

clue.text: Somebody‘s mum pinched by sexist?

indicators.note: to pinch is to squeeze between fingers, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a sexist is one kind of bigot
mum as in keeping quiet; SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A mother being groped by a chauvinist man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not a mother but the word for silence, as in 'keep mum'. 'Somebody' is a noun meaning an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: To be a somebody is to be a person of importance, and a big shot is an influential or important person.

clue.text: Mark‘s first wife overlooked by brother

indicators.note: in a down entry, whatever overlooks another piece sits above it and is read earlier

blocks.note: BR is an abbreviation for brother
Eve was the first woman and wife in the Bible

explanation.surface: A man named Mark whose first wife was ignored by his brother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is a written sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is the curved diacritic sign placed over a vowel to show it is short, so it is a written mark.

clue.text: Old scientist from Middle Eastern lake, briefly over

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: the Sea of Galilee in Israel, a lake, with its final letter cut
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An ancient researcher who came from a lake region of the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sea of Galilee is really a freshwater lake. O for over comes from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo Galilei was the Italian astronomer and physicist of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: After vacation, homework at uni contains first-class poem

indicators.note: vacating means emptying, so only the outermost letters are kept
to contain is to hold something within

blocks.note: the word with its middle emptied out
A1 means first-class, written with I for 1
U is the first letter of uni, standing for university

explanation.surface: A student's homework, written at university after the holidays, includes an excellent poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacation' looks like a holiday, but here it means emptying out the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese verse form of three lines, so it is a kind of poem.

clue.text: Finally bet on neither odd number

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter is kept
odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are rearranged
in a down entry, one piece on another sits above it

blocks.note: the final letter
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler finally placing a stake on neither odd nor even numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd number' reads as one phrase in a gambling sense, but 'odd' shuffles and 'number' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirteen is a specific whole number, an example of the general category that the clue names.

clue.text: Make laws on introduction of inflammable rubbish

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so just the first letter is taken

blocks.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
the opening letter
to rubbish something is to criticise it harshly, to slate it

explanation.surface: Passing laws about dealing with rubbish that could catch fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' equals LEG only via cricket, where the on side and leg side are the same half of the field. 'Rubbish' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is for a parliament or ruling body to pass statutes, which is precisely making laws.

clue.text: Prime letters for clueing a single Italian

indicators.note: prime numbers are 2, 3, 5 and 7, so the letters in those positions are kept

blocks.note: the 2nd, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters
a single is one, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Choosing the best letters for writing a crossword clue about one Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime' looks like it means best, but it means prime-numbered positions in the word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi is a common Italian given name, standing here for an Italian man, a typical crossword example.

clue.text: Important vitamin fed to young animal

indicators.note: whatever is fed to something is taken inside it, so one piece enters another

blocks.note: a foal is a young horse
vitamin C

explanation.surface: An essential vitamin supplement given to a newborn animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Important' opens the clue looking like a description of the vitamin, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something focal is central, the point of greatest attention, and so it is of chief significance.

clue.text: Extreme difficulty with fit on small loose garment

indicators.note: one thing placed on another follows it in the reading order of this entry

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
an ordeal is often called hell
to fit is to suit, as in a colour that suits you

explanation.surface: Struggling badly to get a small-sized baggy item of clothing to fit.
explanation.walkthrough: A shell suit is a shiny, lightweight nylon tracksuit popular in Britain around 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell suit is a baggy two-piece tracksuit with a crinkly nylon outer shell, worn loose over the body.

clue.text: Socrates’ usual complicated challenge for division?

indicators.note: something complicated has been tangled up, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: the philosopher's name, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A typically knotty philosophical puzzle set by Socrates about how to divide things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Division' suggests arithmetic, fitting the philosophy picture, but it means an army division.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault course is an obstacle circuit that soldiers must complete, so it is a test set for a military unit.

clue.text: College works to introduce new electronic notes?

indicators.note: to introduce something is to bring it in, so a piece goes inside the rest

blocks.note: a tech is a technical college
N is the standard abbreviation for new
OP, short for opus, is a work; two of them make works

explanation.surface: A college using its projects to bring in a new electronic system for taking notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like written memos, but it is musical notes; N slips between the college and the pair of works.
explanation.definitionFit: Technopop is pop music made largely with synthesisers, so it is electronically produced musical sound, with the question mark flagging the loose definition.

clue.text: Intelligent European principle

blocks.note: rational means able to reason
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.walkthrough: The three words read as a phrase, but the last is the definition and the first two build the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reasoning or fundamental basis for a course of action, much like a guiding principle.

clue.text: Savings at an end: it stops celebrity backing spender with lowbrow tastes

indicators.note: at an end points to the final position, so only the last letter is kept
going backwards runs the letters from end to start
a stopper plugs a hole, so these letters are pushed inside another piece

blocks.note: the final letter
'it' is an old euphemism for sex or sex appeal
a celebrity is a big name

explanation.surface: A spendthrift with no savings left, backing a celebrity until the money runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: S and SEX together go into the reversed NAME. Essex man is a British stereotype: a brash, newly affluent working-class man from the county of Essex, near London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essex man caricature was coined for a flashy big spender, keen on consumer goods, with supposedly unsophisticated, vulgar tastes.

clue.text: Pervert acts as his mood changes

indicators.note: when something changes its form is altered, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the thirteen letters, taken as written

explanation.surface: A deviant whose behaviour shifts along with his mood swings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pervert' could be a verb, but it is the noun and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who takes pleasure in giving and receiving pain is widely regarded as having a sexual perversion.

clue.text: Marshall in LA worked with 25

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or processed, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written
the solution to 25 across

explanation.surface: A US marshal, a law officer in Los Angeles, who worked alongside a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshall' suggests a lawman, but it is the first name of the media theorist; the cross-reference brings in the painter from 25.
explanation.definitionFit: Marshall McLuhan was the Canadian media theorist famous for 'the medium is the message', so his first name identifies him.

clue.text: Hush after street leaves complaint

indicators.note: whatever leaves departs, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: a hush is a quiet calm
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Quiet returns once the noisy street empties, and someone files a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' looks like a grievance, but it is a medical complaint. ST comes off the front.
explanation.definitionFit: In medical usage a complaint is an ailment or disorder, which is another word for sickness or disease.

clue.text: One who fails to beat king and queen

blocks.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A player who cannot defeat the king and queen, as in chess or cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' is the verb to thrash; 'and' simply joins the royal pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To tank is informal for to fail badly or lose deliberately, so a person who tanks falls short.

clue.text: Line-up so worried about Times sacking?

indicators.note: worried means fretted over, so the letters are disturbed into a new order
about means around, so these letters surround another piece

blocks.note: taken as written, hyphen dropped
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: Staff at The Times anxious about a round of dismissals in the line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper that publishes this very puzzle, but it is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacking is dismissal from a job, and expulsion is the act of forcing someone out.

clue.text: Anxiety relating to certain countries that’s not his

indicators.note: not means without, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: Hispanic means relating to Spain and Spanish-speaking countries
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: Worry about foreign countries that are not one man's own.
explanation.walkthrough: Deleting the three letters from the front of the word leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, an extreme form of anxiety and nervous alarm.

clue.text: State bore recalled stopping Nixon regularly

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters run backwards
at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept
a stopper plugs a gap, so these letters sit inside another piece

blocks.note: bore as the past tense of bear, meaning had
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: A tedious state official recalled from office in the Nixon era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person, but it is the past tense of bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the states of the USA, in the north-west, so it is an example.

clue.text: John with odd bits of foam sponge

indicators.note: odd positions are first, third and so on, so those letters are kept

blocks.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is loo
the first and third letters

explanation.surface: A man named John with a bit of bath foam on his sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a name but is slang for a toilet; the British loo means the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofa is the dried fibrous pod of a gourd, used in the bath to scrub the skin like a sponge.

clue.text: Artist‘s champ

blocks.note: first meaning: the Norwegian painter of The Scream
second meaning: to chew noisily

explanation.walkthrough: 'Champ' looks like a champion, but it is the verb for chewing noisily; the 's means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Munch the painter is a famous artist, and to munch is to chew food steadily and audibly, as a horse champs.

clue.text: Brandy man on beer, drinking very quietly

indicators.note: whatever drinks takes something inside it
one piece placed on another comes after it in this entry

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet
Jack is a stock name for a man, as in every man jack

explanation.surface: A man drinking brandy on top of beer, but doing it very discreetly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very quietly' is a musical dynamic, pianissimo, written as a doubled p on a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Applejack is an American spirit distilled from cider, which makes it a kind of apple brandy.

clue.text: Party enforcing six-pack ban? It’s not possible

blocks.note: a six-pack holds cans, so banning it means no can
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party where the hosts forbid people bringing beer in six-packs? Impossible.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in reverse order to the clue; the question mark flags the whimsical reading of a no-cans party.
explanation.definitionFit: No can do is an informal idiom used to refuse a request, meaning that something cannot be done.

clue.text: Old Frenchman‘s grazing cattle finally moving forward

indicators.note: the last letter is shifted to an earlier slot, so it goes back inside the rest

blocks.note: to pasture cattle is to put them out grazing

explanation.surface: A French farmer of old, whose cattle were grazing and finally advancing across the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The final E of the grazing word moves forward two places.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the nineteenth-century French chemist and microbiologist, a Frenchman of a past era.
